title: ICALL-BENCH: Benchmarking LLM Interprocedural Reasoning in Binary Programs
title_zh: ICALL-BENCH：基准测试大语言模型在二进制程序中的过程间推理能力

paragraphs.en: ICALL-BENCH以间接调用目标恢复为探测手段，评估LLM对二进制程序过程间语义的推理能力，成功率介于23%至81%。 Recent benchmarks show that LLMs achieve strong performance in both function-level binary understanding and end-to-end binary reverse engineering tasks, but whether LLMs can reason over interprocedural semantics in compiled binaries remains unclear. Function-level benchmarks offer limited visibility into cross-function relationships, while whole-program benchmarks typically evaluate final outcomes of tasks that may be solvable from local clues alone, making it difficult to disentangle interprocedural reasoning from exploration, tool use, execution, and retrieval. To address this limitation, we introduce ICALL-BENCH, a benchmark that directly evaluates whether LLMs and agents can understand and reason over interprocedural semantics in binary programs, using indirect-call target recovery as a measurable probe. ICALL-BENCH covers 50 complete real-world C/C++ programs spanning different complexity levels and multiple optimization configurations, with an average of 74,746 lines of code and 941 functions per program. We further introduce three analysis regimes spanning model-only reasoning, static tool-augmented agents, and Internet-enabled open-world agents to examine how intrinsic reasoning, active information acquisition, and external knowledge each contribute to interprocedural binary analysis. We evaluate five recent LLMs and their corresponding agents. Our results reveal a wide separation across current models and agents, with program-level verifiable success rates ranging from 23% to 81%. They also show that greater information access does not consistently lead to better results, with particularly limited gains on the hardest cases, where deeper interprocedural reasoning remains the primary bottleneck. Uneven performance across models and frequent verifiable failures even under an optimistic evaluation indicate that robust binary interprocedural reasoning remains an open challenge.
paragraphs.zh: 近期基准测试表明，LLM在函数级二进制理解与端到端二进制逆向工程任务中均表现出色，但LLM能否对编译后二进制程序的过程间语义进行推理仍不明确。 函数级基准测试对跨函数关系的可见性有限，而全程序基准测试通常评估的是仅凭局部线索即可求解的任务的最终结果，难以将过程间推理与探索、工具使用、执行和检索区分开来。 为解决这一局限，我们提出ICALL-BENCH，该基准以间接调用目标恢复作为可度量的探测手段，直接评估LLM和智能体能否理解并对二进制程序中的过程间语义进行推理。 ICALL-BENCH涵盖50个完整的真实世界C/C++程序，跨越不同复杂度级别和多种优化配置，平均每个程序包含74,746行代码和941个函数。 我们进一步引入三种分析模式，涵盖仅模型推理、静态工具增强的智能体以及具备互联网访问能力的开放世界智能体，以考察内在推理、主动信息获取和外部知识各自对过程间二进制分析的贡献。 我们评估了五个近期LLM及其对应的智能体。 我们的结果显示当前模型与智能体之间存在巨大差距，程序级可验证成功率介于23%至81%之间。 结果还表明，更大的信息获取量并不总能带来更好的结果，在最难的案例上收益尤为有限，而更深层次的过程间推理仍是主要瓶颈。 各模型表现参差不齐，且即使在宽松的评估条件下仍频繁出现可验证的失败，这表明鲁棒的二进制过程间推理仍是一个开放性挑战。
